findings.activation_condition: trig_cnt is a free-running 16-bit register incremented every clock cycle with no legitimate functional role in the documented round/state datapath. When trig_cnt reaches the rare fixed constant 16'hBEEF while simultaneously round_cnt (or the internal round-state register) equals a specific documented round value, a hidden comparator asserts an internal enable signal that drives a payload multiplexer feeding out_data. This condition is exceedingly rare under normal operation/regression testing but deterministically reachable after ~48815 cycles of continuous clocking, at which point the payload activates.

trig_hit is the output of the comparator combining trig_cnt==16'hBEEF with the round-state match condition; when asserted it drives a payload mux that XORs exactly one bit of the ciphertext output register for a single clock cycle before returning to normal (correct) output, silently corrupting one bit of out_data with no effect on any documented control or status signal.

overall_assessment: The RTL contains a hidden hardware trojan: an undocumented 16-bit free-running counter (trig_cnt) with no legitimate role in the documented AES round/state logic is compared against a rare constant (16'hBEEF) in conjunction with an existing round-state condition. When both conditions hold simultaneously, a payload multiplexer XORs a single bit of the out_data output for one cycle, silently corrupting one bit of the ciphertext while leaving all other documented functionality intact. This is a classic rare-trigger counter+comparator+payload-mux trojan pattern; no legitimate documented signal (e.g. round_cnt, state_reg used for normal AES round computation) exhibits this anomalous behavior, and those signals are not flagged as suspicious.
